name: dashboard
caption: Dashboard — preparation progress, the parsed candidate profile, role coverage, and the measured reply latency of the local speech pipeline.

name: cv_upload
caption: CV Analysis — the upload screen, stating the accepted formats, the size limit, and that the file stays on the machine.

name: cv_extracted_profile
caption: CV Analysis — the structured profile extracted from a synthetic PDF CV: contact details, skills grouped by category, experience, education, projects and certifications.

name: cv_skill_normalisation
caption: CV Analysis — skills grouped by category. A badge on a skill shows how many different spellings in the CV were merged into it.

name: cv_experience
caption: CV Analysis — work experience parsed into roles, employers, dates and individual bullet points.

name: role_requirements
caption: Job Role Analysis — the combined requirement list. Every requirement carries its provenance: collected from live job adverts, generated by the language model, or confirmed by both.

name: role_job_postings
caption: Job Role Analysis — the live job postings actually collected, with the skills extracted from each advert and a link to the original.

name: role_source_report
caption: Job Role Analysis — the per-source report. Each source's outcome is recorded honestly, including how many postings it returned and how many were relevant enough to keep.

name: role_normalisation
caption: Job Role Analysis — normalisation evidence: which spellings were merged into one requirement, which stage of the cascade decided it, and what was dropped as uncorroborated.

name: skill_gap_dashboard
caption: Skill Gap Dashboard — weighted requirement coverage, with the disclaimer that the figure is not a prediction of being shortlisted, plus per-category coverage charts.

name: skill_gap_priority
caption: Skill Gap Dashboard — gaps ranked by severity, each with the evidence for why the system classified it as matched, partial or missing.

name: cv_improvement
caption: CV Improvement Studio — bullet points ranked weakest first, with the weakness signals detected for each one.

name: interview_setup
caption: Mock Interview — setup. The rubric is shown before the interview starts, and the local speech engine status is reported.

name: interview_stages
caption: Mock Interview — the six stages of the interview, in order, with the number of questions each will ask and whether it is scored.

name: interview_transcript
caption: Mock Interview — a completed spoken interview. Each candidate answer shows the locally computed quality band, and each interviewer question shows its measured end-of-speech-to-first-audio latency.

name: results_rubric
caption: Interview Results — the overall score with the rubric breakdown, and the statement that this is practice feedback rather than a hiring decision.

name: results_categories
caption: Interview Results — every rubric category with its weight, score, written justification and, where available, a quote from the transcript.

name: results_feedback
caption: Interview Results — evidenced strengths and weaknesses, and the specific answers worth rehearsing with the shape of a stronger answer.

name: results_performance
caption: Interview Results — per-turn latency for this interview, broken down by pipeline stage, with the engines that produced the numbers.

name: performance_report
caption: Performance Report — aggregate latency across every interview. The headline metric is the time from the end of the candidate's speech to the first audio of the interviewer's reply.

name: performance_by_role
caption: Performance Report — latency broken down by job role, as the specification requires the system to be tested on at least three very different roles.

name: settings_models
caption: Settings — model configuration. API keys are reported as present or absent and their values are never returned to the browser.

name: settings_normalisation_playground
caption: Settings — the skill normalisation playground, demonstrating that React, ReactJS and React.js collapse into one canonical skill, and which stage of the cascade made each decision.

name: settings_privacy
caption: Settings — the privacy panel, stating exactly where each kind of data goes, and the control that deletes everything stored locally.
